newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Assembly meets for first time since election.
newsitem.headline: French Assembly meets for first time since election.

text.p: France's National Assembly met on Thursday for a first time since the left swept to power last week and was set to elect Socialist former prime minister Laurent Fabius as speaker.
The oldest member of the parliament, 85-year-old centrist Charles Ehrmann, presided over the opening session of the 577-member assembly elected in a two-stage vote on May 25 and June 1.

"I declare the...legislature open," Ehrmann told the Assembly, which includes 62 women, up from 37 in the outgoing legislature. He was accompanied on the podium by the six youngest parliamentarians, starting with Victor Brial, 31.
Members of the Assembly were to vote for speaker, the main task of the opening session.

Fabius, backed by the Socialists and their Communist allies, was strong favourite be chosen as speaker, a post he held in the early 1990s. Fabius was France's youngest prime minister at the age of 37 when he began two years in the post in 1984.

The election was likely to go to a second round because ecologists, angry over the Socialists' refusal to grant one of their members the chairmanship of the assembly's laws committee, put up their own candidate, Guy Hascoet.

Parties in the ousted centre-right coalition were also presenting rival candidates in a new sign of disarray after the snap election called by conservative President Jacques Chirac backfired on his allies.

The Rally for the Republic party (RPR), founded by Chirac, was fielding Nicole Catala. But the Union for French Democracy, rating her too sceptical towards European integration, presented its outgoing floor leader Gilles de Robien.
Once elected, the new speaker traditionally reassures deputies that he will serve them all equally.
New Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is due to make his keynote policy address on June 19 promising to give top priority to fighting France's record 12.8 percent unemployment.
Outgoing National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin is set to take over as RPR party leader from former prime minister Alain Juppe.
